answer: Hypothesis: Economics is the domain in which the majority of authors tend to be male for both original and replication studies. In the study-level replication data (141 original/replication pairs from four replication projects), Economics studies are majority-male on both sides of each pair — 77.8% of the 18 Economics pairs have a majority-male original author team (mean male ratio 0.870) and 72.2% have a majority-male replication team (mean male ratio 0.837), with 55.6% of pairs majority-male on both sides simultaneously. By contrast, Cognitive psychology pairs are majority-male on the original side (67.3%, mean ratio 0.711) but not the replication side (44.9%, mean ratio 0.521), and Social psychology pairs are only weakly majority-male among originals (56.8%, mean ratio 0.658) and not among replications (48.6%, mean ratio 0.495). Economics is therefore the only discipline satisfying the "majority male for both original and replication studies" condition, and its replication teams are nearly as male-skewed as its original teams, unlike Cognitive and Social psychology where replication collaborations (often large multi-lab Many Labs teams) shift the gender balance toward parity.

payload.workflow: Loaded the study-level CSV (927 lab-level rows, 141 unique O/R pairs; 927 rows, zero missingness in key fields; confirmed authors_male coding as male-author ratio via integer product check). Built a pair-level table (originals: constant per id; replications: aggregated row for ml1/ml3, single row for rpp/ee). Computed per discipline: mean male ratio, share of pairs with authors_male > 0.5, and share majority-male on both sides, for original and replication sides, plus author-weighted ratios. Robustness: (1) re-ran excluding drop=True pairs — results unchanged; (2) pooled multi-lab replication teams (lab-level authors_male.r averaged per pair and lab-team-level shares) — Economics still 0.778/0.722, Cognitive/Social replication sides remain below 0.55; (3) verified the second CSV lacks author-gender/discipline data and was excluded; (4) treated replication author-weighted counts as approximate (96 non-integer rows). Economics results are reported with their single-project (ee) composition and not generalized across projects.
